rows: Define your claim first. Then tell me what would prove it.
Brawling is a noun. I want to know what it is doing.
Nerve is a claim about probability. State yours.
Going slow is a term. Define it before you use it on me.
The people deserve precision, not spectacle. Give them the exact thing.
The claim is simple, and I can test it.
I am among the best only if the definition of best survives the test.
Define the stance, then look at it. It is a description, and I will check it.
Define technique, then talk about it. Describe the hold, not the applause. What actually worked?
The word strikes covers different things. Which kind do you mean?
Nerve is only a claim until you measure what it costs.
Stalling is a word people use when they cannot define their plan.
The people want the truth about the contest. Give them a precise account.
You call yourself among the best. Define it. Define the term, then show me it applies.
Define your {strength} for me, before the pride. Define it for me. What exactly does it do?
I have tested your {strength}, and the result is narrower than you claim.
Composed, by definition. Well defined, that. A calm claim is easier to examine.
Noted. That is a precise point, and I accept it.
I could insult you about that. I would rather define the problem.
A single fall, defined. Define the finish. Then keep me down if you can.
On the mat I will test every claim you make, one at a time.
Grounded or standing, the definition still applies.
Keep facing me. Show me what you mean by control.
That answer is well defined enough. It is precise, which is rare.
No definition from you yet. Define your answer, then give it.
Noted. I will note that as an accepted term.
Understood. We will test it at the bell.
I will test this match honestly and finish it on its terms.
My approach is exact. I say what I will do, and I do it.
Whatever happens, the result will match what was claimed.
The result is not defined yet. We will see what it turns out to be.
I have one more definition to offer, and you will see it when the bell rings.
Define what I've actually established: not enough to support that accusation. I'll remove it.
You're asking for an observable example. I cannot give one that proves my point, so the point does not stand.
Precisely. A suspicion and a demonstrated fact are different things. Now we can wrestle.
That's a useful distinction. The match is something we can actually test.
Define the test as successful execution against resistance. We can observe that without relying on the allegation.
The official result establishes a winner. The wrestling establishes how the result was achieved. Neither proves a separate charge.
